newsitem.title: USA: Chateau spurns Zell, Sun offers, for revised ROC deal.
newsitem.headline: Chateau spurns Zell, Sun offers, for revised ROC deal.

text.p: Chateau Properties Inc. Wednesday spurned two takeover offers from rival mobile home park operators in favour of a revised merger deal with its original partner ROC Communities Inc.

Since Chateau signed a merger agreement with ROC in July, Sun Communities Inc. and Chicago developer Samuel Zell's Manufactured Home Communities Inc. have approached the real estate investment trust with their own offers.

Chateau said it rejected Manufactured Home's $400 million, $26 a share, offer as inadequate and said the long-term benefits of a combination with ROC were superior to a merger with Sun, which offered $390 million.

Chateau said the "revised merger agreement with ROC is the best alternative for Chateau stockholders and represents the opportunity for both superior long-term value and strategic and operational benefits."
Under the revised ROC deal, Chateau shareholders would receive a greater amount of stock per Chateau share in the new company to be formed in the so-called merger of equals.

Clinton Township, Mich.-based Chateau also said it planned to buy back up to 1.45 million of its common shares, about 24 percent of its outstanding stock. ROC said it would purchase as many as 350,000 Chateau shares before the merger.
The amended deal also lowered the Chateau votes needed to approve the merger to a simple majority of shares, rather than two-thirds.

The combined company will be renamed Chateau Communities Inc. and will be based at ROC's current offices in Englewood, Colo. The legal structure of the merger will be modified so that ROC will merge into a newly-formed subsidiary of Chateau.

Under the revised deal, each Chateau common share will be exchanged for 1.0316 shares of the combined entity, rather than one share as originally planned. The exchange ratio for ROC stockholders was unchanged at 1.042.

Chateau also will allow holders of limited partnership interests to exchange those units into common shares. The effective exchange ratio could increase if holders of those units opt to exchange them into common stock.
Chateau said assuming that 70 percent of the 8.8 million outstanding partnership units were exchanged, for example, the effective exchange ratio for Chateau stockholders would be about 1.06.

Holders of limited partnership interests including Chateau Chairman John Boll and Chateau director Edward Allen, have said they plan to exchange up to 6 million, about 68 percent, of the partnerhip units for Chateau common stock, the companies said. Another 2.8 million of the units units may also be exchanged.

Chateau said it filed a lawsuit against Manufactured Home on Tuesday, alleging that the company's bid violated federal securities laws, that it began a proxy solicitation to foil Chateau's merger with ROC by making material misstatements of facts and failing to disclose other material facts.
The suit was filed in the U.S. District Court for the District of Maryland.

Chateau said it also faces a class action suit filed on Sept. 12 alleging that its directors violated their fiduciary duties to stockholders by agreeing to the merger with ROC and refusing to endorse the Manufactured Home offer.
Chateau's stock fell $1.375 to $25.25 and ROC slid 25 cents to $23.875 on the New York Stock Exchange in afternoon trading.
